post.caption: Shackleton tossed his gold into the snow. In October 1915, Shackleton's ship, Endurance, was wrecked in the ice. Every man could keep only two pounds of personal gear. Shackleton threw a handful of gold sovereigns into the snow. He also left behind a Bible from Queen Alexandra. First, he tore out the flyleaf and a few pages to keep. Seaman Tom McLeod picked the Bible up and kept it. It reached the Royal Geographical Society in 1971. One exception to the rule was Leonard Hussey's banjo.
